title: Retirement lifecycle and customer migration flow for deprecated model versions
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable, low-friction retirement workflow for old model versions that minimizes customer disruption while preserving observability and cost goals. This ticket codifies notice cadence, in-console and API signals, migration guide requirements, pinning semantics, performance-profile deprecation behavior, and rollback paths.

Scope: Applies to any model variant or performance profile we plan to retire from the public catalog (hosted + dedicated manifests). Excludes emergency takedowns (handled by incident runbooks). Covers communication templates, console UX banners, SDK/API headers for deprecation, migration guide checklist, telemetry to surface affected customers, and engineering gating for the sunset.

High-level lifecycle (proposed):
- Announcement window: 90 days prior to sunset for major/backwards-incompatible changes; 30 days for minor profile tweaks.
- Early-warning: Automated email + in-console banner + billing notice to org admins at 90/60/30/7 days.
- Migration phase: Provide migration guide + recommended replacement model/version + performance delta table and token-cost comparison.
- Pinning & compatibility: Customers pinned to a given model version will continue to be served until designated sunset date but will receive a warning header on API responses: "X-Model-Deprecation: version=foo; sunset=2026-06-01; migration=https://...". Document retention: pinned metadata visible in console per-route.
- Forced removal: If necessary (security/critical bug), follow incident escalation; otherwise, final shutdown after end-of-life date with 7-day emergency notice and one-time migration assistance for paid customers.

Required migration guide contents (template):
- Overview: Why the version is sunset and recommended target(s).
- Compatibility checklist: breaking changes, tokenization differences, logits/temperature semantics, supported features (functions, streaming), quantization caveats.
- Performance profile delta: 95th latency, median latency, token-cost per 1k tokens for both old and recommended model under representative workloads.
- Quality notes: examples of prompt changes or reranking steps to retain output quality.
- SDK/code diffs: minimal patch examples for REST/SDK clients and common frameworks.
- Rollback plan: how to pin back to previous version temporarily and telemetry to watch.
- Acceptance tests: small set of unit/eval prompts customers can run to validate parity.

Operational responsibilities:
- PM (owner): final approval of notice cadence, migration guide, customer outreach templates.
- Eng (runtime/infra): ensure deprecation header and console flag, gating checks for dependent features, and automated scripts to list pinned customers.
- Design (DX): banner copy, email templates, and migration guide layout.
- Support/CS: playbook for inbound requests, SLA for assisted migrations for paid plans.
- Legal/Compliance: sign-off for any contractual obligations on Dedicated/Private customers.

Telemetry & success metrics (what to measure):
- Number of orgs affected and percentage migrated before sunset.
- Error spike rate / 4xx/5xx for routes tied to retired model.
- Cost delta observed post-migration for migrated customers.
- Support tickets created per 100 affected orgs.
- Time-to-migration (median days from first notice to traffic cutover).

Console & API UX changes required:
- Console: per-model "EOL" banner with countdown, link to migration guide, button to request assisted migration. Show pinned routes flagged in routes list.
- API: add optional response header X-Model-Deprecation and runtime warning in streaming protocol metadata. Include replacement model id and sunset epoch.

Rollback and safety nets:
- Allow org admins to opt into extended support windows (manual approval).
- Maintain a hot-standby of the last compatible runtime image for 30 days after sunset for emergency pinning.
- Automated revert job for customers who report functional regressions within 7 days of migration (rate-limited).

Open questions / decisions needed:
1) Standard notice window: adopt 90/60/30/7 by default or make configurable per-model?
2) Do we automatically map performance profiles to replacement defaults or leave recommendation to model owners?
3) For Dedicated/Private customers, what contractual notification period is required vs hosted? (legal needs to confirm)
4) What telemetry gate indicates we should extend sunset for a subset of customers? (e.g., >5% of pinned traffic fails sanity checks)

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Finalized notice cadence and template copy.
- Migration guide template (markdown) and one worked example for model-family "xgen-medium-16k".
- PR adding X-Model-Deprecation header and console flags (ENG-4021).
- Support playbook + canned responses.

Acceptance criteria:
- Template and example migration guide published in Confluence.
- Console shows EOL banner for models marked for retirement in staging.
- API returns deprecation header for pinned-version traffic in staging.
- At least one dry-run migration executed with internal beta org and documented outcomes.

Potential risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Mass customer churn if communication is unclear. Mitigation: staged comms, offer assisted migration and capacity for support.
- Risk: Unexpected latency difference post-migration. Mitigation: precompute perf-profile deltas and include rollback path.

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the human and operational workflow; the deep implementation details (kernel compatibility checks, runtime compatibility matrix) are tracked in ENG-4167 and ENG-4021.
